slot.brief: Direct use of αΔT for volume/length expansion of a metal rod or liquid by a given amount; straightforward plug-in.

stem: A liquid of volume $1.5\times10^{-3}$ m$^3$ is heated through $20^\circ$C. If its coefficient of volume expansion is $4.0\times10^{-4}\ ^\circ$C$^{-1}$, what is the increase in its volume?
working:
$\Delta V=V\beta\Delta T$\\
$=1.5\times10^{-3}\times4.0\times10^{-4}\times20=1.2\times10^{-5}\ \text{m}^3$\\
$1.2\times10^{-5}\ \text{m}^3=12\ \text{mL}$

Independent check: ΔV = βVΔT = (4.0×10⁻⁴)(1.5×10⁻³)(20) = 12×10⁻⁶ m³ = 12 mL.
solution:
The increase in volume is $[?]$
$$
\Delta V=V\beta\Delta T=(1.5\times10^{-3})(4.0\times10^{-4})(20)=1.2\times10^{-5}\text{ m}^3=12\text{ mL}.
$$
